title: Polite Requests with Si and the Imperfect Subjunctive

sections.title: Putting a request at a distance
sections.content: You know *¿Podría ayudarme?* and *Me gustaría…* from A2 Unit 26, where the conditional softens a request. At B2 you add a more formal step. A request wrapped in *si* + the imperfect subjunctive is not a real condition: it puts the request at a distance, so the other person can say no without awkwardness. A conditional verb such as *agradecería* or *sería* can also be followed by *que* + the imperfect subjunctive, the same pair of tenses you know from *si tuviera…, viajaría* in B1 Unit 4. All of these use *usted* forms.

sections.title: Four polite patterns
rows: Si fuera tan amable de + infinitive
If you would be so kind as to…
I would be grateful if you …
It would be better if we …

items.spanish: Si fuera tan amable de esperar un momento, el director lo recibirá enseguida.
items.english: If you would be so kind as to wait a moment, the director will see you right away.

items.spanish: Si tuviera un momento, me gustaría hacerle una pregunta.
items.english: If you had a moment, I would like to ask you a question.

items.spanish: Le agradecería que me enviara el contrato antes del viernes.
items.english: I would be grateful if you sent me the contract before Friday.

items.spanish: Sería mejor que lo habláramos mañana.
items.english: It would be better if we talked about it tomorrow.

sections.content: After *tan amable de* the verb is an infinitive. After *que* it is in the imperfect subjunctive: *que me enviara*, not *que me envía*. Compare a real condition such as *Si no le importa, abro la ventana*: with the present, you will simply do it unless the other person objects.
